title: proto_hep Module
content_markdown: The **proto\_hep** module is a transport module which implements hepV1 and hepV2 UDP-based communication and hepV3 TCP-based communication. It also offers an API with which you can register callbacks which are called after the HEP header is parsed and also can pack sip messages to HEP messages.The unpacking part is done internally.
overview: The **proto\_hep** module is a transport module which implements hepV1 and hepV2 UDP-based communication and hepV3 TCP-based communication. It also offers an API with which you can register callbacks which are called after the HEP header is parsed and also can pack sip messages to HEP messages.The unpacking part is done internally.
how_it_works:
Once loaded, you will be able to define HEP listeners in your configuration file by adding their IP and, optionally, a listening port. You can define both TCP, UDP, and TLS listeners. On UDP you will be able to receive HEP v1, v2 and v3 packets, on TCP and TLS only HEPv3.

...
#HEPv3 listener
socket= hep\_tcp:127.0.0.1:6061 		# change the listening IP
#HEPv1, v2, v3 listener
socket= hep\_udp:127.0.0.1:6061 		# change the listening IP
...

exported_parameters.name: hep_id
exported_parameters.description:
Specify a destination for HEP packets and the version of HEP protocol used. All parameters inside **hep\_id** must be separated by **;**. The parameters are given in key-value format, the possible keys being **uri**, **transport** and **version**, except destiantion's URI which doesn't have a key and is in **host:port** . **transport** key can be **TCP**, **UDP** or **TLS**. **TCP** and **TLS** works only for HEP version 3. **Version** is the hep protocol version and can be **1**, **2** or **3**.

HEPv1 and HEPv2 can use only UDP. HEPv3 can use TCP, UDP and TLS having the default set to TCP. If no hep version defined, the default is version 3 with TCP and TLS.

NO default value. If **hep\_id** the module can't be used for HEP tracing.

exported_parameters.name: homer5_on
exported_parameters.description: Specify how the data should be encapsulated in the HEP packet. If set to _0_, then the JSON based HOMER 6 format will be used. Otherwise, if set to anything different than _0_, the plain text HOMER 5 format will be used for encapsulation. On the capturing node, this parameter affects the behavior of the _report\_capture_ function from the [sipcapture](sipcapture#func_report_capture) module.

exported_parameters.name: homer5_delim
exported_parameters.description: In case **homer5\_on** is set (different than 0), with this parameter you will be able to set the delmiter between different payload parts.

exported_parameters.name: hep_port
exported_parameters.description: The default port to be used by all TCP/UDP/TLS listeners.

exported_parameters.name: hep_send_timeout
exported_parameters.description: Time in milliseconds after a TCP connection will be closed if it is not available for blocking writing in this interval (and OpenSIPS wants to send something on it).

exported_parameters.name: hep_max_msg_chunks
exported_parameters.description: The maximum number of chunks in which a HEP message is expected to arrive via TCP. If a received packet is more fragmented than this, the connection is dropped (either the connection is very overloaded and this leads to high fragmentation - or we are the victim of an ongoing attack where the attacker is sending very fragmented traffic in order to decrease server performance).

exported_parameters.name: hep_async
exported_parameters.description: Specifies whether the TCP connect and write operations should be done in an asynchronous mode (non-blocking connect and write) or not. If disabled, OpenSIPS will block and wait for TCP operations like connect and write.

exported_parameters.name: hep_async_max_postponed_chunks
exported_parameters.description: If hep_async is enabled, this specifies the maximum number of HEP messages that can be stashed for later/async writing. If the connection pending writes exceed this number, the connection will be marked as broken and dropped.

exported_parameters.name: hep_capture_id
exported_parameters.description: The parameter indicate the capture agent ID for HEPv2/v3 protocol. Limitation: 16-bit integer.

exported_parameters.name: hep_retry_cooldown
exported_parameters.description: This parameter defines how many seconds OpenSIPS should wait before retrying a TCP connection to the HEP destination after reaching the maximum number of failed attempts set by hep_max_retries. Limitation: 16-bit integer.

exported_parameters.name: hep_max_retries
exported_parameters.description: This parameter defines the maximum number of attempts OpenSIPS will make to establish a TCP connection with the HEP destination. Limitation: 16-bit integer.

exported_parameters.name: hep_async_local_write_timeout
exported_parameters.description: If _hep_async_ is enabled, this specifies the number of milliseconds that a write op will be tried in blocking mode (optimization). If the write operation lasts more than this, the write will go to async mode and will be passed to bin MAIN for polling.

exported_functions.name: correlate

parameters.name: hep_id
parameters.description: the name of the _hep_id_ defined in modparam section, specifying where to do the tracing.

parameters.name: type1
parameters.description: the key name identify the first correlation id.

parameters.name: correlation1
parameters.description: the first extra correlation id that will be put in the extra correlation chunk.

parameters.name: type2
parameters.description: the key name identify the second correlation id.

parameters.name: correlation2
parameters.description: the second extra correlation id that will be put in the extra correlation chunk.

exported_functions.description: Send a hep message with an extra correlation id containing the two correlation given as arguments. The two types must differ. This will help on the capturing side to correlate two calls for example, being given their callid as correlation ids.
